subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Vectors: parallel vectors and geometric applications
Transformation geometry: reflection, rotation, translation and enlargement
Transformation geometry: describing and applying transformations

questions.q: In a column vector, what does the top number represent?
options: The angle the vector makes with the horizontal
questions.explain: A column vector is written with the horizontal component (x) on top and the vertical component (y) underneath.

questions.q: What does the notation |a| mean for a vector a?
options: The magnitude (length) of the vector a
The direction of the vector a
The negative of the vector a
questions.explain: The modulus notation |a| denotes the magnitude, or length, of the vector a.

questions.q: Which single piece of information fully describes a translation?
options: A centre and a scale factor
A centre, an angle and a direction
questions.explain: A translation is completely described by a single column vector giving the horizontal and vertical shift.

questions.q: To fully describe a rotation you must state the centre, the direction and which other quantity?
questions.explain: A rotation requires a centre, an angle of turn and a direction (clockwise or anticlockwise).

questions.q: Which single feature is needed to describe a reflection?
questions.explain: A reflection is fully described by giving the equation of its mirror line.

questions.q: Which two pieces of information are required to describe an enlargement?
options: A centre of enlargement and a scale factor
A mirror line and a scale factor
A column vector and a centre
questions.explain: An enlargement is described by its centre and its scale factor.

questions.q: Which transformation does NOT, in general, preserve the size of a shape?
questions.explain: Reflection, rotation and translation produce congruent images, whereas an enlargement changes the size (unless the scale factor is 1 or -1).

questions.q: What is the result of the vector addition (2, 3) + (4, -1)?
questions.explain: Vectors are added by summing the corresponding components: 2+4 = 6 and 3+(-1) = 2.

questions.q: What is 3 multiplied by the vector (2, -1)?
questions.explain: Multiplying a vector by a scalar multiplies each component: 3x2 = 6 and 3x(-1) = -3.

questions.q: How does the vector -a compare with the vector a?
options: Same direction but twice the magnitude
Opposite direction and half the magnitude
questions.explain: Negating a vector keeps its length the same but reverses its direction.

questions.q: Two non-zero vectors are parallel if and only if one is:
options: A scalar multiple of the other
Equal in magnitude to the other
The negative reciprocal of the other
questions.explain: Parallel vectors point in the same or opposite direction, so one can always be written as a scalar multiple of the other.

questions.q: Under a reflection in the line y = x, the point (a, b) maps to:
questions.explain: Reflection in y = x swaps the x- and y-coordinates.

questions.q: A rotation of 90 degrees anticlockwise about the origin maps the point (x, y) to:
questions.explain: A 90 degree anticlockwise rotation about the origin sends (x, y) to (-y, x).

questions.q: An enlargement with scale factor -1 about a point is equivalent to which transformation about that same point?
questions.explain: A scale factor of -1 produces an image the same size but inverted through the centre, identical to a 180 degree rotation about that centre.

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (5, 12)?
questions.explain: The magnitude is the square root of (5^2 + 12^2) = square root of 169 = 13.

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (6, 8)?
questions.explain: The magnitude is the square root of (6^2 + 8^2) = square root of 100 = 10.

questions.q: Under an enlargement of scale factor 2, centre the origin, the point (3, -2) maps to:
questions.explain: With centre the origin, each coordinate is multiplied by the scale factor: (2x3, 2x-2) = (6, -4).

questions.q: The point (1, 2) is translated by the vector (3, -5). What are its new coordinates?
questions.explain: Add the translation vector to the coordinates: (1+3, 2+(-5)) = (4, -3).
